extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners (attorneys, agents), and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and required elements for filing U.S. patent applications (nonprovisional and provisional), including inventor oaths/declarations, fees, incorporation by reference, ADS use, required copies/translations, and conversion to provisional. Focused on compliance to avoid abandonment and secure a filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postponement of inventor's oath or declaration (apps filed on/after Sep 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, applicants may postpone filing the inventor's oath or declaration until the application is otherwise in condition for allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective December 18, 2013, an oath or substitute statement in compliance with 37 CFR 1.63 or 1.64 must be filed no later than the date the issue fee is paid to avoid abandonment. This time period is not extendable under 37 CFR 1.136 (see 37 CFR 1.136(c)). The Office may dispense with the notice under 37 CFR 1.53(f)(1) if each required oath/declaration or substitute statement has been filed before the application is in condition for allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.53(f)(1) — Notice for missing fees or oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application does not contain the basic filing fee, the search fee, the examination fee, or the inventor's oath or declaration (and applicant has provided a correspondence address), 37 CFR 1.53(f)(1) provides for a notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must pay the basic filing fee, search fee, examination fee, and pay the surcharge if required by 37 CFR 1.16(f) within the time period set in the notice to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.53(f)(2) — Missing parts when no correspondence address provided
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant has not provided a correspondence address and the application lacks the basic filing fee, search fee, examination fee, or inventor's oath/declaration, the applicant must pay required fees and any surcharge within three months from the filing date to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This three-month period is measured from the filing date when no correspondence address is present.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.53(f)(3) — Timing and surcharge for delayed oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.53(f)(3) sets forth the time period for filing the inventor's oath or declaration and conditions under which filing may be postponed until the application is in condition for allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing the oath/declaration may be postponed only under conditions in 1.53(f)(3)(i)-(ii). Payment of the surcharge under 37 CFR 1.16(f) is required if the inventor’s oath/declaration is not submitted on filing. The surcharge cannot be postponed until a Notice of Allowance issues or payment of the issue fee but must be paid in the time period specified in 1.53(f)(1) or (f)(2). If the surcharge is not paid at filing, the Office will send a Notice to File Missing Parts requiring the surcharge.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.53(f)(3)(i) — ADS and inventor identification requirement for postponement
rubrics_metrics.description: To postpone filing the oath/declaration under 1.53(f)(3)(i), the application must be an original (non-reissue) application that contains an application data sheet (ADS) in accordance with 37 CFR 1.76 identifying each inventor by legal name and a mailing address where the inventor customarily receives mail (and residence if different).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant must file an oath/declaration in compliance with 37 CFR 1.63, or substitute statement in compliance with 37 CFR 1.64, executed by or with respect to each actual inventor no later than the date on which the issue fee is paid. See 35 U.S.C. 115(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: No Notice to File Missing Parts when fees, surcharge, and signed ADS present
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application under 37 CFR 1.53(b) does not include the inventor's oath/declaration but does contain the applicable filing fees (basic filing fee, search fee, examination fee, any excess claims fee, and any application size fee), the surcharge required by 37 CFR 1.16(f), and a signed ADS providing the information required by 1.53(f)(3)(i), the Office will not issue a Notice to File Missing Parts requiring the oath/declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensuring all listed fees, the surcharge, and a signed ADS are present on filing avoids a Missing Parts notice for the oath/declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to File Missing Parts when fees/surcharge/ADS absent
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application under 37 CFR 1.53(b) that does not contain the inventor's oath/declaration also does not contain the applicable filing fees, or the surcharge, or a signed ADS with the required information, the Office will issue a Notice to File Missing Parts giving the applicant a time period (usually two months) to file the missing parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the inventor's oath/declaration will not be required to be filed within the period for reply to the Notice to File Missing Parts if the applicant provides a signed ADS with required information, any required filing fees and surcharge must be filed within the reply period to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice Requiring Inventor's Oath or Declaration when application is in condition for allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is in condition for allowance but does not include an oath/declaration in compliance with 37 CFR 1.63 or substitute statement in compliance with 1.64 executed by each inventor, the Office will issue a Notice of Allowance and Fee(s) Due together with a Notice Requiring Inventor's Oath or Declaration requiring the applicant to file the oath/declaration no later than the date of payment of the issue fee to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant receives the notice and fails to file a proper reply before or with payment of the issue fee, the application will be regarded as abandoned. See 37 CFR 1.53(f)(3)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑AIA (pre‑Sep 16, 2012) missing parts and oath/declaration rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications accorded a filing date that do not include the appropriate filing fee, search fee, examination fee, or oath/declaration, the applicant will be notified under pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.53(f) and given a period to file the missing parts and pay the surcharge under 37 CFR 1.16(f) to prevent abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The oath/declaration filed in reply must be executed by the inventors and must identify the specification and any amendment filed with the specification which includes subject matter not otherwise included in the specification (including claims) or drawings. Amendments filed with the oath may not include new matter; if an oath improperly refers to an amendment containing new matter, a supplemental oath deleting the reference will be required under pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.67. Alterations made prior to execution of the oath and filing are considered part of the original disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 111(a) — Required contents of a patent application
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for patent shall be made in writing and shall include: (A) a specification as prescribed by section 112; (B) a drawing as prescribed by section 113; and (C) an oath or declaration as prescribed by section 115.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application shall be accompanied by the fee required by law. The fee, oath or declaration, and one or more claims may be submitted after the filing date within such period and under such conditions (including payment of a surcharge) as prescribed by the Director; failure to submit within the prescribed period will result in abandonment. The filing date is the date on which a specification, with or without claims, is received in the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.57 — Incorporation by reference (reference filing) conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to the conditions and requirements of 37 CFR 1.57(a), a reference made in English in an ADS upon filing of an application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) to a previously filed application (identifying the prior app by application number, filing date, and authority/country) shall constitute the specification and any drawings of the later application for purposes of a filing date under 37 CFR 1.53(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference filing replaces the current application's specification and drawings with those of the previously filed application for filing‑date purposes. Specific requirements and follow-up (copies, translations, fees, surcharge) apply under 1.57(a)(1)–(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.57(a)(1) — Notification and required submissions when ADS reference and correspondence address provided
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant has provided a correspondence address, the applicant will be notified and given a period within which to file a copy of the specification and drawings from the previously filed application, an English translation if necessary (and pay the §1.17(i) fee), and pay the surcharge required by §1.16(f) to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a notice may be combined with a notice under 37 CFR 1.53(f) (e.g., requiring at least one claim and payment of filing fees).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.57(a)(2) — Three‑month period when no correspondence address
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant has not provided a correspondence address, the applicant has three months from the filing date of the application to file a copy of the specification and drawings from the previously filed application, an English translation if necessary, pay the §1.17(i) fee if applicable, and pay the surcharge required by §1.16(f) to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This three-month rule parallels the missing‑parts timing in 1.53(f)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of abandonment under 37 CFR 1.57(a)(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application abandoned under 1.57(a)(1) or (a)(2) shall be treated as having never been filed, unless the application is revived under §1.137 and a copy of the specification and any drawings of the previously filed application are filed in the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely supply required copies/translations/surcharges effectively nullifies the filing date unless revived and corrected under the specified petition/revival procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.57(a)(4) — Certified copy requirement and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A certified copy of the previously filed application must be filed in the Office unless the previously filed application is filed under 35 U.S.C. 111 or 363, or the previously filed application is a foreign priority application meeting conditions in §1.55(i). The certified copy, if required, must be filed within the later of four months from the filing date of the application or sixteen months from the filing date of the previously filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not filed within that period, the certified copy must be accompanied by a petition showing good and sufficient cause for the delay and the petition fee per §1.17(g). The certified copy ensures that the copy later provided corresponds exactly to the previously filed foreign application; the interim copy provision of §1.55(j) does not apply to this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference filing does not by itself establish priority/benefit claims
rubrics_metrics.description: In a reference filing under 37 CFR 1.57(a), the reference to a previously filed application in an ADS is not sufficient to establish a priority or benefit claim to that previously filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference filing information is provided in a section of the ADS separate from the foreign priority and domestic benefit claim sections. See MPEP §§211 and 213 for domestic benefit and foreign priority claims guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADS recommended and governs over PLT Model forms when inconsistent
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of an ADS to supply application information for reference filing is encouraged; information in an ADS will govern when inconsistent with information supplied in PLT Model forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicants want to postpone submission of the inventor's oath or declaration until condition for allowance, an ADS providing inventor information is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of actual copy of previously filed application — no modifications allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: In response to a notice requiring a copy of the specification and drawings from the previously filed application, applicants must submit an actual copy of the specification (including any claims) and drawings without any modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the specification and drawings submitted in response are modified (updated, corrected, or reformatted), they will not satisfy the copy requirement of 35 U.S.C. 111(c) and 37 CFR 1.57(a). Any desired changes must be made by amendment under 37 CFR 1.121 without adding new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and revival for reference filing abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: An application abandoned under 37 CFR 1.57(a)(1) or (a)(2) is treated as having never been filed; it may be revived under 37 CFR 1.137 and a copy of the specification and drawings of the previously filed application submitted to the Office to cure the defect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant may claim priority or benefit only if the application is revived under 37 CFR 1.137 and the required copy is submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of ADS reference metadata required
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants filing by reference should ensure that the application number, filing date, and intellectual property authority or country of the previously filed application are accurately specified on the ADS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the ADS specifies incorrect application number, filing date, or authority/country, the applicant may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.53 to have the application accorded a filing date as of the date the intended specification and drawings are filed using those papers. Simply submitting the intended specification and drawings in reply to a 1.57 notice without such a petition will be treated as an incomplete reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference filing intended only when copy not available; surcharge applies if reference used
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference filing is intended for situations when a copy of the previously filed application is not available at the time the current application is filed; if a copy is available, the applicant should file the copy under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) and 37 CFR 1.51(b) rather than use reference filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reference filing section of the ADS is completed, applicants will be charged the surcharge under 37 CFR 1.16(f) even if a copy of the previously filed application is submitted on filing. A reference filing statement made upon filing cannot be rescinded because the reference constitutes the specification and drawings of the instant application (35 U.S.C. 111(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: No provision for continuation‑in‑part via reference filing
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no provision under 37 CFR 1.57(a)/35 U.S.C. 111(c) for filing a continuation‑in‑part of a previously filed application by reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference filing 'shall constitute the specification and any drawings of the subsequent application'; because a C‑I‑P must extend beyond the previous specification, filing by reference for a C‑I‑P is not contemplated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application filing date and amendment limits (post‑Dec 18, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application filed on or after December 18, 2013 will be given a filing date as of the date a specification, with or without claims, is received in the Office. Amendments, other than those required to make the provisional comply with applicable regulations, are not permitted after the filing date of the provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For provisional applications filed prior to December 18, 2013, filing date rules follow pre‑PLT 37 CFR 1.53(c). See MPEP §601.01(f)/(g) for treatment of omitted drawings or missing figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.53(e) — Missing specification or drawings in provisional
rubrics_metrics.description: When the specification or drawing are omitted, 37 CFR 1.53(e) requires that the applicant be notified and given a time period in which to submit the missing element to complete the filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§601.01(f) and (g) for applications filed without drawings or without all figures of drawings, respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional cover sheet and identification requirement (37 CFR 1.53(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: All provisional applications must be filed with a cover sheet, which may be an application data sheet (37 CFR 1.76) or a cover letter identifying the application as a provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will treat an application as filed under 1.53(b) unless the application is clearly identified as provisional. A provisional identified as such but lacking a complete cover sheet per 1.51(c)(1) will be treated as provisional but must submit the complete cover sheet and a surcharge later in conformance with 1.53(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional missing cover sheet or fee — 1.53(g) notice and two‑month period
rubrics_metrics.description: When the provisional application does not have a complete cover sheet or the appropriate fee, the applicant will be notified pursuant to 37 CFR 1.53(g) and given a time period (usually two months) to provide the necessary fee or cover sheet and to pay the surcharge under 37 CFR 1.16(g) to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This time period may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136(a). If the filing fee is not timely paid, the Office may dispose of the provisional application. If no correspondence address provided, applicant has two months from the filing date to file the basic filing fee, cover sheet, and pay the surcharge per 1.16(g) to avoid abandonment. Copies of a provisional will be provided by the USPTO upon request and payment of the fee unless the provisional has been disposed of.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic filing fee requirement for provisional if later used for 119(e) benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: The basic filing fee must be paid in a provisional application on filing or within the time period set forth in 37 CFR 1.53(g) for the provisional to be entitled to a filing date under 37 CFR 1.53(c) if any claim for benefits under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) based on that application is made in a subsequently filed nonprovisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.78 for benefit-claim procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of refusal to accord a filing date — petition requirement (37 CFR 1.53(e)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for review of a refusal to accord an application a filing date must be made by way of a petition accompanied by the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §506.02 for petition practice guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion from nonprovisional to provisional (37 CFR 1.53)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for patent filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) may be converted to a provisional application and be accorded the original filing date of the nonprovisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request for conversion must be accompanied by the processing fee under §1.17(q) and be filed prior to the earliest of: (i) abandonment of the nonprovisional; (ii) payment of the issue fee on the nonprovisional; or (iii) expiration of twelve months after the filing date of the nonprovisional. Grant of conversion does not entitle applicant to a refund of fees properly paid in the original application.
